body:
1. Spring vs. Spring Boot

Spring is a comprehensive framework for Java development that requires manual configuration (XML or Annotations). Spring Boot is an extension of Spring that offers auto-configuration and embedded servers to get applications running faster.

2. Dependency Injection (DI)

A design pattern where the Spring IoC Container provides the objects (dependencies) a class needs, rather than the class creating them itself. This promotes loose coupling.

3. Inversion of Control (IoC) Container

The core of the Spring Framework. It manages the lifecycle of Java objects (Beans), including instantiation, configuration, and destruction.

4. Bean Scopes

Spring supports several scopes, most notably: Singleton (one instance per container - default) and Prototype (new instance every time it is requested).

5. @SpringBootApplication

A convenience annotation that combines three others: @Configuration (tags the class as a source of bean definitions), @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan.

6. Spring Boot Starters

A set of convenient dependency descriptors. For example, spring-boot-starter-web automatically pulls in all dependencies needed for web development, including Tomcat and Spring MVC.

7. Auto-Configuration

Spring Boot looks at the classpath and the beans you have defined to automatically configure your application. If it sees HSQLDB on the path, it automatically configures an in-memory database connection.
